section1.title: 1. What Are Parameters and What Do They Do?
section1.p1_desc: The normal duration a worker is supposed to work in a day. The system divides the personnel's daily wage by this value when calculating the hourly wage.
section1.p2_desc: Determines the coefficient by which the standard hourly wage will be multiplied in case of overtime. The standard coefficient in labor law is usually 1.5.

section2.title: 2. Work Types and Multipliers
section2.p1_desc: The manner in which the personnel is present on site that day.
section2.p2_desc: The rate at which the selected work type affects the daily wage (e.g., Full Day x1.0, Half Day x0.5, Sunday Overtime x1.5 or x2.0).

section3.title: 3. Timesheet and Calculation Formula
section3.p1_desc: The digital chart recording the days and overtime hours actually worked by the workers.
section3.f_total: Total Earnings = Base Earnings + Overtime Pay
section3.f_base: Base Earnings = Daily Wage * Work Type Multiplier
section3.f_hourly: Hourly Wage = Daily Wage / Standard Working Hours
section3.f_overtime: Overtime Pay = Hourly Wage * Overtime Multiplier * Overtime Hours
section3.example: Example: Wage 2,000, Full Day (x1), 2 Hrs Overtime (x1.5), Std Hours (8). Result: 2,000 (Base) + 750 (Overtime) = 2,750.

section4.title: 4. Rules for Accurate Data Entry
section4.p1_desc: Enter the daily net and full wage.
section4.p2_desc: Select the correct status for that day.
section4.p3_desc: Do NOT enter normal working hours in the "Overtime" field; only enter additional working hours performed outside standard hours.
section4.p4_desc: The system will warn you if you enter a timesheet for days on leave.

about.faq_q1: Does Tecton need an internet connection?
about.faq_a1: No. The database lives on this computer and every module works offline. An internet connection is only used to check for updates.
about.faq_a2: In %APPDATA%/Tecton/elektronik-yevmiye.sqlite. Tecton also keeps rotating backups in the same folder and, if you connect one, a snapshot in your cloud folder.
about.faq_q3: How do I move Tecton to a new computer?
about.faq_a3: Connect a cloud folder or create a full backup in Settings, install Tecton on the new computer, then restore that backup. The application restarts with your records in place.
about.faq_q4: How does cloud backup work without an account?
about.faq_a4: Tecton writes a JSON snapshot into a folder that OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive or Nextcloud already syncs. No account, server or subscription is involved.
about.err_name_empty: Row {line}: Full Name cannot be empty.
about.hero_subtitle: Construction site operating system for Windows
about.hero_desc: Tecton keeps sites, people, payroll, materials and cash in one offline desktop application. Every record stays on this computer and, only if you connect one, in the cloud folder you choose.
about.faq_q5: Can I change the language and the theme later?
about.faq_a5: Yes. Settings offers 19 interface languages, 14 themes plus a custom colour, a selectable icon and interface zoom from 80% to 150%.
about.faq_a6: Tecton checks GitHub Releases, downloads only the changed blocks, verifies the SHA-512 signature and installs silently when you confirm. Microsoft Store builds never update themselves.
about.help_desc: Short answers to the questions that come up most often.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Site/Workspace Management?)
q1.desc: A management panel that allows you to define physical locations where your projects are executed and separate data on a site-specific basis.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Project Site Data Stored?)
q2.desc: All added project sites and all transactions linked to these sites are stored in the local database.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should a New Project Site be Defined?)
q3.desc: It should be defined in the system as soon as a new physical site is opened or before any subcontractor/personnel assignments are made.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Select, Reorder, and Manage Sites?)
q4.desc: Add a new site using the form, drag-and-drop items in the list to reorder them, and click 'Select Workspace' to set a site active.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Create Site-Based Workspaces?)
q5.desc: To report all daily journals, timesheets, cash transactions, and material movements independently without mixing them up.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage the Project Sites List?)
q6.desc: Company owners, general coordinators, and headquarters executives can define, edit, or delete project sites.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Personnel Management?)
q1.desc: A tracking system that monitors the attendance, advances, progress earnings, and OHS document status of blue-collar and white-collar employees working on your site.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Personnel Data Stored?)
q2.desc: All employee cards, groups, and ledger transactions are stored in the local database, filtered by your active project site.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When to Add Personnel and Log Attendance?)
q3.desc: New employees are registered when they start. Attendance and advance entries should be logged daily or weekly without delay.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Add Personnel and Import/Export Excel?)
q4.desc: Click 'Add Personnel' in the top right to create a card; download the template for bulk data entries and import from Excel with one click.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Track Personnel in Detail?)
q5.desc: To prevent salary discrepancies, avoid missing OHS document expiration dates, and calculate the real-time labor cost of the site correctly.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage the Personnel List?)
q6.desc: Project managers, site chiefs, and administrative officers can define new employees, create groups, and manage attendance/advances.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Quantity Survey tracking?)
q1.desc: A tracking system that measures physical progress in the project by recording quantities and units (m², m³, ton, etc.) of completed on-site works.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Production Data Kept?)
q2.desc: Data is stored in the local database. You can add specific locations like blocks, floors, or axes in the description/notes area.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should Production be Logged?)
q3.desc: As daily works are completed or when quantity/progress calculations are made, they must be recorded on a daily basis without delay.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Query Production Data?)
q4.desc: Use the search bar to search by item name or notes; filter the list by date range and unit types.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Track Quantity Surveys?)
q5.desc: To calculate project completion rates, verify subcontractor progress payments, and ensure compliance with the planned schedule.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Log Production entries?)
q6.desc: Site chiefs, quantity survey engineers, or project supervisors can add new production records and update existing ones.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Material Delivery Tracking?)
q1.desc: A tracking system that digitally records the quantity, unit (m³, ton, kg, etc.), supplier name, and physical delivery note documents of construction materials received on site.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Delivery Records Stored?)
q2.desc: Material records are stored in the local database, while uploaded invoice or receipt photos are securely stored under your local project folder.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should Deliveries be Recorded?)
q3.desc: Immediately when the supplier vehicles deliver the materials to the site and the physical delivery note is signed.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Upload Receipt Photos?)
q4.desc: By selecting files from your PC or scanning the QR code with your mobile camera to transfer them wirelessly via the local area network (LAN).

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep Material Records?)
q5.desc: To verify supplier invoices, track instantaneous material consumption (concrete, rebar, etc.), and prevent loss or theft of construction assets.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Log Material Entries?)
q6.desc: Site chiefs, warehouse managers, project engineers, or administrative staff can add new delivery notes and edit historical entries.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is a Daily Journal?)
q1.desc: A daily journal is an official record where daily weather conditions, active worker counts, and all site activities, deliveries, and events are recorded chronologically.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are these Records Stored?)
q2.desc: Journal records are stored in the local SQLite database and filtered based on the active project (workspace).

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should the Journal be Recorded?)
q3.desc: It should be recorded at the end of each work day or concurrently. Date filters allow easy historical search.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How are Weather and Worker Counts Fetched?)
q4.desc: Weather is automatically fetched via OpenWeather based on project location. Worker counts are autonomously calculated from the daily timesheets.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Daily Journal?)
q5.desc: To build a historical, official, and verifiable archive for future labor disputes, progress payments, or subcontractor claims.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage These Records?)
q6.desc: Site managers or authorized personnel can edit. For data integrity, editing is only allowed for the current day's record.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Quality Control Tracking?)
q1.desc: A digital reporting system that records technical defects, faulty, or missing construction activities with photo evidence and tracks them until resolved.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are these Records Kept?)
q2.desc: Records are stored in the local database, isolated under the active project. Specific locations (blocks, floors) can be detailed in the description.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should a Report be Created?)
q3.desc: Instantly when a defect or quality issue is identified on site. Once the issue is corrected, its status is changed to 'RESOLVED'.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Upload Photos?)
q4.desc: By selecting files from your computer or wirelessly using the local network (LAN) mobile photo uploader via QR code.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep Quality Reports?)
q5.desc: To guarantee compliance with construction specifications, document subcontractor/worker liability for faulty work, and prevent future technical or financial claims.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage These Reports?)
q6.desc: Site managers, control engineers, or quality inspectors can open and close reports. All modifications are autonomously tracked in the system audit logs.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Subcontractor Ledger?)
q1.desc: A current account tracking system that monitors the names, contact info, daily wage rates, and financial debit/credit balances of subcontractors (excavation, ironwork, catering, etc.) on your site.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Data Stored?)
q2.desc: All subcontractor cards and ledger transactions are stored in the local database. They are isolated and filtered on a project basis.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When to Enter Ledger Transactions?)
q3.desc: Transactions should be recorded immediately when a progress billing is earned or a payment/advance is made. OHS documents should also be kept updated based on expiration dates.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Manage Progress Billings and Payments?)
q4.desc: Click the detail button next to the subcontractor card to access their profile; add new progress billings and payments to automatically calculate the net balance.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Subcontractor Ledger?)
q5.desc: To prevent manual errors in subcontractor and machine rental accounts, view net debit/credit status in real-time, and automatically track OHS document durations.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage Subcontractor Accounts?)
q6.desc: Site chiefs, accounting officers, and project managers can define new subcontractors, enter progress billings/payments, and share account statements via WhatsApp.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is the Media Gallery?)
q1.desc: A visual archive center that collects all photos uploaded during material deliveries (delivery notes) or quality reports under one roof.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Media Files Stored?)
q2.desc: Images are securely stored on the local disk under your project folder. The database only keeps their relative file paths.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When are Images Added?)
q3.desc: They are added concurrently when progress/quality reports are written or material receipt notes are saved.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Filter and Search Media?)
q4.desc: You can search by title using the search bar, and filter by sorting (date), content type (delivery note / report), or photo status.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Photo Archive?)
q5.desc: To visually prove construction quality on-site, digitally back up the physical delivery notes, and quickly resolve retrospective disputes.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Use the Media Gallery?)
q6.desc: All authorized project team members, including site managers, control engineers, administrative staff, and project owners, can view it.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Cash Register Management?)
q1.desc: A financial tracking system that records all cash inflows (income/advances) and cash outflows (expenses/subcontractor payments) of the projects.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Cash Records Stored?)
q2.desc: Data is securely stored in the local database. Transactions can be filtered and reported for 'Headquarters' or individual project sites.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should Transactions be Recorded?)
q3.desc: Instantly when a payment is made, an advance is issued, or progress payment is received.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Query and Report Cash Data?)
q4.desc: Filter by date range, project, transaction type, or description; export reports instantly in Excel, CSV, JSON, or PDF format.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Cash Register?)
q5.desc: To monitor real-time cash flow, view net balance status, manage personnel/subcontractor current accounts accurately, and prevent budget overruns.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage Cash Operations?)
q6.desc: Project managers, finance staff, and site chiefs can insert transactions. Deletion operations are audited via confirmation modals.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is the Recycle Bin?)
q1.desc: A recovery system that temporarily holds accidentally deleted construction sites, personnel records, cash transactions, delivery notes, daily journals, and quality reports.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Deleted Data Kept?)
q2.desc: Deleted data is not permanently erased. It is marked with a soft-deleted flag in the local database and listed on this page.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When Can I Restore Data?)
q3.desc: You can restore any deleted item at any time after its deletion. There is no expiration date or automatic purge cycle.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Restore and Search Data?)
q4.desc: Click the 'Restore' button on the right side of the list to recover data in seconds. You can filter by date, record type, and project.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why is the Recycle Bin Needed?)
q5.desc: Designed to prevent permanent data loss due to accidental deletions under intense site work conditions and to maintain complete traceability.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Recover Data?)
q6.desc: Authorized site managers, engineers, or account owners who have delete/restore privileges in the application can initiate the recovery process.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Subcontractor Statement Tracking?)
q1.desc: A detailed date- and note-based statement breakdown of the works completed (progress billing) and payments/advances made to a subcontractor.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Transactions Stored?)
q2.desc: Current account transactions are stored in the local database. Logged payments are automatically integrated into the Cash Register page.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When to Add Progress Billings and Payments?)
q3.desc: Progress billings should be entered when work is delivered by the subcontractor, and payments/advances should be recorded simultaneously when paid.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Export and Share via WhatsApp?)
q4.desc: You can generate reports using the date range filters, download them as PDF/Excel with one click, or share them directly via WhatsApp.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Detailed Statement?)
q5.desc: To prevent accounting discrepancies and double payments with subcontractors, and to report the company's net debt liabilities without errors.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage This Profile Page?)
q6.desc: Authorized site managers, project coordinators, and accountants can add or delete progress billings and payments.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What are System Logs?)
q1.desc: A digital ledger system that records critical database operations (create, update, delete), background events, and potential errors chronologically.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Log Files Kept?)
q2.desc: System logs are stored locally on your disk. They are completely offline and never sent to any external server or cloud provider.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When are Logs Written?)
q3.desc: Written autonomously with millisecond precision the exact instant a user performs an action or when an application error is caught.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Inspect Logs?)
q4.desc: Use the search bar to filter, or filter by log type to view Info (blue), DB Create (green), DB Update (yellow), or DB Delete/Error (red).

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep System Logs?)
q5.desc: To track user modifications (audit logs) retrospectively, locate the exact root cause of errors, and maintain security.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Access the Logs?)
q6.desc: Only the administrator running this instance or authorized support engineers with access to the local machine can read these logs.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Bulk Timesheet Entry?)
q1.desc: An autonomous fast-entry system that allows logging timesheet details (wages, overtime, notes) for multiple personnel working on the same site on the same day in one go.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where are Timesheets Stored?)
q2.desc: Timesheet records for all selected workers are stored as separate rows in the database. Each record directly updates that worker's current account statement.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When should Bulk Timesheets be Logged?)
q3.desc: At the end of the day, shift end, or before progress payment cycles for prompt tracking of the entire active workforce.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Log Bulk Timesheets?)
q4.desc: Select personnel from the left panel (with search and 'Select All' support), specify the date, work type (Full Day, Half Day, etc.) and overtime on the right panel, and click 'Save All'.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Use Bulk Timesheet Entry?)
q5.desc: To eliminate the tedious task of entering timesheets individually for dozens of workers on large sites, save time, and minimize entry errors.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage Bulk Timesheets?)
q6.desc: Authorized site chiefs, timesheet clerks, administrative officers, or project managers can perform bulk timesheet entries.

q1.title: 1. WHAT? (What is Personnel Statement Tracking?)
q1.desc: A current account statement containing the breakdown of the selected employee's worked days (attendance), earned wages, received advances, and leave history.

q2.title: 2. WHERE? (Where is Data Stored?)
q2.desc: All attendance, advance, and leave records are stored in the local database. Payments are automatically integrated into the Cash Register page.

q3.title: 3. WHEN? (When to Log Attendance and Advances?)
q3.desc: Attendance is logged daily when work is completed. Advances or weekly payments are recorded immediately when paid.

q4.title: 4. HOW? (How to Export and Share via WhatsApp?)
q4.desc: Use the date range filters to generate the statement, download it as PDF/Excel with one click, or share it directly with the employee via WhatsApp.

q5.title: 5. WHY? (Why Keep a Detailed Personnel Ledger?)
q5.desc: To definitively resolve salary or advance disputes at the end of the month and to prove the accuracy of historical progress payments.

q6.title: 6. WHO? (Who Can Manage the Personnel Profile Page?)
q6.desc: Authorized project managers, site chiefs, or accounting staff can add/delete attendance, advances, and leaves.

onboarding.tour_nav: The left rail groups every module: sites, people, operations, finance and system.
onboarding.tour_spotlight: Press Ctrl + K anywhere to jump to any page.
onboarding.tour_backup: Your data is backed up automatically to this device and to your cloud folder.

cloud.title: Cloud backup
cloud.safe_fallback: No cloud folder found. Data is kept in {{path}}.
cloud.sync_failed: Cloud sync failed. Your local data is unaffected.
cloud.restore_confirm: Replace the current data with the cloud backup?

update.title: Updates
update.store_managed: Updates are managed by the Microsoft Store.
update.dev_build: Update checks are available in the installed version.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.subtitle: A practical manual for every module, plus the shortcuts and backup rules that keep your data safe.
docs.hotkey_desc: The global shortcut works even while Tecton is minimised to the tray.
docs.cloud_desc: Tecton writes a daily snapshot to your cloud folder, keeps the previous file and rotates 15 daily backups. The newest valid copy is used when a file is damaged.
docs.support_desc: Copy a diagnostic summary (version, Windows build, database size, cloud status) to paste into a support request. No personal records are included.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.subtitle: Publisher, licence and privacy information for Tecton.
legal.privacy_body: Tecton works offline. Your site, payroll, material and cash records stay in the local database on this computer and, only if you connect one, in the cloud folder you choose. There is no Tecton account, no telemetry and no third-party analytics.
legal.terms_body: Tecton is provided as is, without warranty. You are responsible for the accuracy of the records you enter and for keeping backups. The MIT licence permits commercial use, modification and redistribution provided the copyright notice is kept.
legal.third_party_body: Tecton is built with Electron, React, Vite, SQLite, i18next, lucide-react, jsPDF and SheetJS. Each component keeps its own licence; the full list is available in the repository.
legal.contact_body: Questions, bug reports and feature requests are handled through the GitHub repository. For commercial support, contact the publisher directly.

integrations.local_api_desc: MCP, the command line and webhooks share one loopback address. Nothing is exposed to the network.
integrations.enable_desc: Turn off to revoke every MCP client and CLI session immediately.
integrations.copy_failed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
integrations.cli_desc: Read status, sites, personnel, cash and the local manual from PowerShell or Terminal.
integrations.mcp_desc: Paste this block into Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf or Cline to give the assistant read access to Tecton.
integrations.mcp_hint: The server speaks MCP over stdio and only reads data through the local API.
integrations.webhooks_desc: Send signed events to a URL you control. Every delivery includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature.
integrations.no_hooks: No webhook yet. Add one below to receive events.
integrations.test_failed: The endpoint did not accept the test delivery.
integrations.save_failed: The webhook could not be saved. Check the address and events.
integrations.start_failed: The local API could not start. Check the system logs.

ai.title: Local assistant
ai.subtitle: Answers come from the built-in manual. With a local model the wording is natural; without one the matching passages are quoted directly.
ai.runtime_missing_desc: Document search already works without it. Install Ollama to let a local model write the answers instead of quoting passages.
ai.tier_light_note: A small model keeps memory use low on 4-8 GB machines.
ai.tier_balanced_note: This computer can run a 3B model comfortably while other apps stay open.
ai.tier_high_note: With this much memory a 7B model gives noticeably better answers.
ai.models_desc: Download one model that fits this computer. You can delete it at any time; the assistant falls back to quoted answers.
ai.downloading: Downloading the model. You can keep working.
ai.download_done: Model downloaded. Activate it to start answering.
ai.action_failed: The action could not be completed. Check that the local runtime is running.
ai.ask_desc: Searches {{count}} built-in sections. No question or record leaves this computer.
ai.ask_placeholder: For example: how do I restore a deleted record?
ai.ask_failed: The assistant could not answer. Try again.
ai.suggest_3: How do I restore a deleted worker?
ai.suggest_4: What does the MCP server expose?
